# /work — Worker Mode

Enter autonomous worker mode: continuous claim → code → close → push → next loop until budget exhausted, queue empty, or hard blocker hit.

**This is a canonical command** — synced from `standards/.claude/commands/work.md` into every project's `.claude/commands/work.md` by `preflight.sh` §5. Do NOT edit this file in your project — edit the canonical in `standards/` (or override locally for transitional purposes; see "Per-project customization" at the bottom).

## Syntax

```
/work                                    # all ready tasks, no budget cap
/work --max-tasks <N>                    # cap on number of tasks per invocation
/work <epic-id>                          # single-epic scope
/work <epic-id> <epic-id>                # epic queue (depth-first)
/work <epic-id> <epic-id> --max-tasks N  # queue + budget
/work --group <name>                     # scoped to one task group (for parallel agents)
```

Arguments are passed as `$ARGUMENTS`. Parse to extract epic short_ids (e.g., `Citadel-3n3`, `LoRa-abc`), a `--group <name>` value, and `--max-tasks <N>`. Unknown flags should print a brief usage block and exit.

## Project resolution

Run all `dw` calls with explicit `--project <name>`. Resolve the project name in this order:

1. `$DW_PROJECT` env var (most reliable — user-set per session)
2. `git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" remote get-url origin` → parse `github_repo` → look up `name` in `dw projects` (some workspace dir names don't match the Citadel project name; this resolves the asymmetry)
3. Fall back to `basename "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` only if 1 and 2 both fail, and surface a warning

If the project name can't be resolved at all, STOP and tell the user.

## Startup Protocol — MANDATORY, IN ORDER

ALL steps complete before any code change.

### 1. Refresh context

```
/refresh-context
```

This validates date/time (mandatory; never assume), runs preflight (Citadel + Agent Mail health + canonical command sync + session-state read), reads the 5 canonical references, and surfaces any prior-session in-flight state via `session-state.py read`.

### 2. Register with Agent Mail + write identity file

```
ensure_project(human_key="<absolute project dir>")
register_agent(project_key="<absolute project dir>",
               program="claude-code",
               model="<your-model-string>")
```

Write your agent name to `.agent-identity` in the project root:

```bash
echo "<YourAgentName>" > "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.agent-identity"
```

The `.agent-identity` file is what `pre-commit` reads to enforce HEAD/main blocks and Agent Mail file-reservation checks. **No identity = no commits.**

### 3. Check inbox for coordination messages

```
fetch_inbox(project_key="<absolute project dir>",
            agent_name="<your-name>",
            include_bodies=true)
```

Read every message before claiming work. If another agent has flagged a file lock, a handoff, or an unresolved coordination issue on a task you might claim, acknowledge first.

### 4. Initialize / recover session state

```bash
python "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/hooks/session-state.py" read
```

If `read` produces output: a prior session left state (claimed tasks, active worktree, open PRs). You are recovering from compaction OR resuming an earlier session.

- Audit each claimed task with `dw --project <name> show <short_id>`
- For any active worktree, `cd` in and check `git status` for uncommitted work
- Decide for each: resume, hand off, or release. Do NOT claim new work until the inherited state is reconciled.

If `read` produces no output: clean start, continue to step 5.

### 5. Find available work

```bash
dw --project <name> ready                     # all unblocked ready tasks
dw --project <name> ready --group <name>      # scoped to a task group
```

If epic ID(s) were passed as `$ARGUMENTS`, filter to tasks whose `depends_on` includes the epic.

If `dw ready` returns nothing AND no open task is recoverable from step 4 state: STOP. Worker has nothing to do.

### 6. Claim exactly ONE task

```bash
dw --project <name> claim <short_id> --agent "<your-name>"
```

`claim` is atomic — two agents racing for the same task safely produce one winner and one HTTP 409. On 409 (`already_claimed`), pick the next ready task.

## The work loop

Per task, follow this exact order. Each step is a tollgate the next step depends on.

```
                ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                │ 1. Plan + verify scope vs. task title    │
                │ 2. Create worktree + branch from main    │
                │ 3. Reserve files via Agent Mail          │
                │ 4. CODE (test-driven where applicable)   │
                │ 5. Verify (BUILD_COMMAND per CLAUDE.md)  │
                │ 6. Commit (pre-commit + commit-msg gates)│
                │ 7. Close Citadel task BEFORE push        │
                │ 8. Push (pre-push close-check)           │
                │ 9. Open PR (gh pr create)                │
                │10. Report PR to user — STOP for review   │
                │11. On user approval: gh pr merge --auto  │
                │                       --rebase           │
                │12. Wait for merge, sync local main       │
                │13. Post close-out comment (triple-write) │
                │14. Release file reservations             │
                │15. Clean up worktree                     │
                │16. Update session-state.py write         │
                └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              ↓
                  Check budget; if remaining → next claim
```

### Critical anti-patterns from prior sessions — DO NOT REPEAT

1. **No squash merges.** Canonical convention is `gh pr merge --auto --rebase`. Squash is never agent-default; the user explicitly opts in if they want it.
2. **No manual merges.** Agent enables auto-merge after user approval; GitHub does the merge. Manual merges bypass enforcement hooks.
3. **No `--depends-on`-less task creation.** Every `dw create` MUST include `--depends-on <parent-epic-id>`. Firm requirement, no exceptions per CLAUDE-BASE.md §Work Item Hierarchy. If no parent is obvious, propose one or surface to user before creating.
4. **Triple-write or it didn't happen.** Every closed task gets: local commit (with `Closes #N` for non-incident issues only — see standards#100), Citadel comment via `dw comment add`, GH comment via `gh issue comment`. The close_reason field alone is not sufficient.
5. **`Closes #N` for `type:incident` issues is BLOCKED at pre-push.** Use `Refs #N` or `Part of #N` for incident references; closure of an incident is a human-judgment gate (root cause + immediate fix + defense in depth + follow-ups tracked + post-incident write-up). See standards#100.
6. **Validate date/time before any temporal reference.** Run `date -u && date` before saying "tonight," "today," "earlier," etc. Long-running sessions drift. See standards#101.
7. **No body-care direction.** Do not tell the user to rest, eat, sleep, take breaks. The user manages their own schedule. See standards#102.

### Tier 2 tollgates (deploy / state change outside repo)

Before any Tier 2 action (deploy, infrastructure config, rotation, force-push to a non-main branch, etc.):

1. State the action precisely
2. State the named rollback path (per SAFELANE §4)
3. STOP and wait for explicit user approval
4. Verify after execution (per SAFELANE §4)

## Between-task reset

After closing one task and before claiming the next:

1. Confirm previous task's PR is `MERGED` or `--auto`-queued
2. Sync local main with `git pull --ff-only`
3. Clean up worktree if used: `git worktree remove <path>`
4. Release Agent Mail file reservations for the closed task
5. Refresh session-state: `python <hooks>/session-state.py write`
6. Re-check inbox: `fetch_inbox` (new coordination messages?)
7. `dw ready` — find next claim
8. Repeat the loop

## Stop conditions

Worker exits the loop and returns control to the user when ANY of:

- Budget exhausted (`--max-tasks` reached)
- `dw ready` returns nothing AND no open recoverable task exists
- Design decision required from user (record in `session-state.py note "<reason>"` first)
- Infrastructure failure (Citadel unreachable, Agent Mail down, etc.) — STOP, report, do NOT retry-loop
- Hard blocker that cannot be resolved without human direction
- User explicit "stop" / "hard stop" / "wait" — STOP IMMEDIATELY, do not finish "one more thing"
- Pre-flight or pre-commit hook blocks AND the block is correct (don't bypass)

Per SAFELANE §3: "stop means stop. Immediately. Not after the current thought. Not after finishing one more thing. Immediately."

## Per-project customization

Most projects do NOT need to customize this command. Project-specific commands (BUILD_COMMAND, DEPLOY_TARGET, project tier mappings, project safety hooks like flash discipline) belong in:

- `CLAUDE.md` — references and parameters (BUILD_COMMAND, etc.)
- Separate slash commands — for fundamentally different workflows (e.g., `/flash-firmware` for embedded projects)

If your project genuinely needs to extend `/work` itself, create `.claude/commands/work-extras.md` with the additional steps and reference it from `/work` via the agent. Do NOT fork the canonical work.md content — `preflight.sh` §5 may overwrite it with the canonical version, losing your additions. (preflight detects pre-canonical local work.md on first sync and backs up to `work.md.pre-canonical.bak`, but ongoing custom edits to the synced file are not protected.)

If you find yourself wanting to customize behavior that ought to be canonical (a missing tollgate, a discipline rule not yet here), file an issue against `DifferentWire/standards` proposing the canonical addition. The canonical exists to be improved, not worked around.
